title: Ordering parts for a job
purpose: How a part gets from the order to the bay, and when an advisor may promise a time.
facts: Parts go on the order from the catalogue with number, brand and tier.
Slot 9 orders for main and east; cover: slot 5 at main, slot 16 at east.
Arrival time is on the order only when the supplier confirmed; a part is "here" when shelved with the order number.
Inter-shop transfers go on the parts manager's 13:00 run (ERP stock_movement: transfers).

Promise rules: on the shelf = a time today; confirmed for a run = that run plus job hours plus one hour; unconfirmed = a call by 14:00; never "same day" on job length alone (S8: slot 7 promised a 3.2-hour job the same day).
Special orders take 2 to 5 working days; over 300 USD needs a deposit.

list_items.item: The part goes on the order from the catalogue: number, brand, tier. Not "front pads".
I order it. East Main: tell me or flag the order. Bonny Oaks: flag the order; I see it. If I am off, Travis orders for East Main and Angie for Bonny Oaks.
VIN first. Always. Half the wrong parts in this building were ordered off a year and a model.
I put the arrival time on the order when the supplier confirms it. Until that time is on the order, there is no time.
The part is "here" when it is on the shelf with the order number on it. Not when the truck is "on its way".
Bonny Oaks gets its parts direct from the supplier. Anything that has to move between the two shops goes on my 1:00 run.
Part on the shelf, technician free: a time today.
Part confirmed for a run: a time after that run plus the job hours plus an hour.
Part not confirmed: "I will call you by 2:00 with a time." Then call.
Never "same day" because the job is only three hours.

new_facts: The 13:00 transfer run; the "run plus hours plus one hour" promise rule; special orders 2 to 5 working days.
